findings.source_quote: καὶ οὐδενὸς δεῖται πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, καὶ προφητειῶν ἀμαυρὰ καὶ ἀμφίβολα, ἵνα ἄλλου προφήτου χρείαν ἔχῃ τὰ λεγόμενα πρὸς ἐπίγνωσιν, ἀλλὰ ῥητὰ καὶ ἁπλᾶ
findings.english_quote: and it needs no one for comprehension; and, of prophecies, obscure and ambiguous things, so that what is said should need another prophet for comprehension, but explicit and plain things
findings.issue: The surviving words are represented and the difficulty is disclosed, but the English leaves the contrasted expressions without an intelligible predication. The genitive προφητειῶν can locally accompany substantivized neuter plurals, so the differing cases alone do not establish corruption. Nevertheless, that local construction does not resolve the governing predication, the purpose clause, and the contrast introduced by ἀλλά. The preceding οὐδενός negates the need for someone or something; it does not by itself establish a following assertion that foreknowledge does not prophesy obscure things. Supplying that assertion would require a separately justified construal or conjecture. The remaining block concerns unresolved clause meaning, not unverified print or the mere existence of interpretive alternatives. The rest of the passage has defensible coverage and wording.
findings.suggested_revision: Preserve the verified reading προφητειῶν. Establish and document a defensible syntactic construal of the entire coordination, including any recoverable predicate and the contrast expressed by ἀλλά, then submit corresponding intelligible English for fresh review. If no such construal can be established, retain the publication block. The proposed replacement καὶ οὐ προφητεύει changes the supplied wording and adds an explicit negation; it must remain identified as an unverified conjecture, not be inserted as though it were the selected edition.
